sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:238494
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 54070 of 2023

Applicant :- Neeresh
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Nagendra Kumar Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Heard Sri P. K. Kashyap Advocate holding brief of Sri Nagendra Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Rajiv Dhar Dwivedi, learned AGA for the State-respondent.

2. The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
259 of 2023, under Sections 306, 498-A, 201 IPC, Police Station Junawai, District Sambhal, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant and his family members on 21.7.2023 under section 498A, 306, 201 IPC and according to the FIR, marriage of the applicant was performed with the daughter of the informant in the year 2015 and on 17.7.2023 an information has been received by the informant that his daughter died under suspicious circumstances and applicant and his family members had taken her dead body for cremation and on this information when informant arrived at cremation point then found that applicant and his family members have already done cremation.

Neeresh vs State Of U.P. on 16 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199223107/
1 4.

Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is husband of the deceased and on the basis of false allegation of abetment he has been made accused in the present matter after four days of the alleged incident.

5. He further submitted that actually deceased died on 17.7.2023 and immediately after the incident applicant informed the informant and his family members and after receiving the information, he participated in the cremation of the deceased and at that time he did not raise any objection but after four days of the alleged incident, he lodged FIR of the present case.
6. He further submitted that it is an admitted case of the prosecution that it is a case of suicide but there is no evidence of abetment against the applicant on record.
7.
He further submitted that applicant is having no criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since 15.8.2023.

8. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the fact that except the fact that applicant is husband of the deceased and without any post mortem dead body of the deceased has been cremated, there is no other evidence against the applicant on record.
9. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

10. However, applicant is the husband of the deceased and it appears that after the death of his wife he also cremated her death body with the help of his family members and neighbours but considering the fact that FIR of the present case was lodged after four days, argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant cannot be completely brushed aside, at this stage that informant and his family members participated in the cremation.
11. Further, applicant is having no criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since 15.8.2023.

12. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
13. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

14. Let the applicant-Neeresh, be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
Neeresh vs State Of U.P. on 16 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199223107/
2

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
15. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

16. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
